snapshot: WHO Western Pacific Region. A large, decentralised health system in the middle of a government-led transformation, with tuberculosis and non-communicable diseases at the top of the agenda.

agenda.title: Free health checks for everyone
agenda.text: The Free Health Check programme (Cek Kesehatan Gratis) is a presidential priority. The minister reported 109 million people screened by October 2026 against a target of 130 million for the year, with blood pressure, blood sugar, cholesterol and body mass index as the first focus. Follow-up is the weak point: reporting in November says only a small share of those diagnosed are in treatment.

agenda.title: Eliminating tuberculosis by 2030
agenda.text: The ministry has restated its 2030 elimination goal and plans 10,600 TB detection devices by 2027. The regulator BPOM is fast-tracking review of the M72 TB vaccine candidate together with the European Medicines Agency, and state vaccine maker Bio Farma is positioning itself as a regional supply hub.

agenda.title: A bid to lead WHO
agenda.text: Indonesia nominated its health minister for WHO Director-General in October 2026. He is one of seven candidates; the World Health Assembly appoints the new Director-General in May 2027.

agenda.title: Health workforce and hospital capacity
agenda.text: Closing the shortage of doctors and specialists is a stated priority, alongside hospital preparedness. WHO reports work with Indonesian hospitals on preparedness and response to antimicrobial-resistant outbreaks.
